decisions.reason: As a training offer that builds directly on the firm’s existing services and application know-how, it likely meets modest aspiration levels and uses slack resources efficiently to support the installed customer base.
This accessory fits the established machinery portfolio and can strengthen system sales, so even if demand is niche the firm would likely retain it unless results clearly fall short of aspirations.

Because it is distant from the firm’s established offer, its performance is more uncertain and a likely shortfall against aspirations would prompt problemistic search and reallocation toward better-fitting activities.
A high-speed CNC milling machine is close to the firm’s core business, supported by strong internal capabilities and a growing market, so management would be inclined to continue it.

The automatic tool change system builds on established products, complements customer productivity goals, and is the kind of incremental innovation a medium-sized German machinery firm would usually keep unless evidence of underperformance becomes clear.
